title: Finite-type extraordinary pullback of potential complexes
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$. Let $f:Y\to X$ be a compactifiable finite-type morphism between Noetherian excellent schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements, def-exc-excellent-ring]. Let $\delta_X$ be a dimension function and let $(K,(p_x))$ be a pinned potential dualizing complex on $(X,\delta_X)$ [def-per-potential-dualizing]. Let $f^!$ denote the right adjoint on bounded-below etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] to ordinary compact-support direct image $Rf_!$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Then
$$\delta_Y(y)=\delta_X(f(y))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(y))}\kappa(y)$$
is a dimension function [def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-weil-residue-field], and $f^!K$ has a natural pinned potential dualizing structure for $\delta_Y$. These pinnings respect composition under the right-adjoint transitivity isomorphism. In particular the normalization is carried by the actual exceptional pullback, not merely by some isomorphic unnormalized dualizing object.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 4.1.2 and Remark 4.1.3; coefficients n=ell

proof.text:
The dimension assertion follows by the dimension-formula argument of Stacks Tag 02JW. $X$ is excellent, hence universally catenary [def-exc-excellent-ring], and so is $Y$, being of finite type over $X$ [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. By [lem-per-immediate-specialization-criterion], on both schemes an immediate specialization $y'\rightsquigarrow y$ in the geometric sense of [def-per-potential-dualizing] is exactly a specialization with $\dim\mathcal O_{\overline{\{y'\}},y}=1$; so it suffices to prove $\delta_Y(y')=\delta_Y(y)+1$ for these, and $\delta_X$ satisfies the same equation for the analogous specializations of $X$. For such $y'\rightsquigarrow y$, restrict to affine neighbourhoods, then to the reduced closures of $y'$ and $f(y')$. These are integral affine schemes given by an inclusion $R\subset B$ of finite-type domains with $R$ universally catenary, by [def-exc-excellent-ring, lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. Write $s'=f(y')$, $s=f(y)$. The height equality of [lem-exc-dimension-formula-universally-catenary-finite-type-domain] gives
$$\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s')}\kappa(y')-\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(y)=\dim\mathcal O_{\overline{\{y'\}},y}-\dim\mathcal O_{\overline{\{s'\}},s}.$$
The first local dimension is $1$. The closure of $s'$ is catenary, so a saturated chain from $s'$ to $s$ has length equal to the second local dimension; each of its steps has one-dimensional local ring of the closure, so the equations for $\delta_X$ add along this chain. Hence $\delta_Y(y')-\delta_Y(y)=1$. All residue extensions have finite transcendence degree because $f$ is finite type. This proves the asserted integer-valued dimension function.

source.place: Tag 02JW, lemma-dimension-function-propagates (morphisms.tex), proof using Tag 02IJ; Zariski versus etale immediate specializations as in ILO Expose XIV, Proposition 2.1.4

proof.text:
We first construct the pinning for any putative $K$. Fix $y\in Y$, $x=f(y)$ and $d_y=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(x)}\kappa(y)$. By [lem-per-exceptional-costalk-calculus] it suffices to work on the fibre $F=Y_x$ and to pin $\pi^!R\Gamma_xK$ at $y$. The reduced closure of $y$ in this fibre has a nonempty regular affine open $U$ containing its generic point: the regular locus is open by the J-2 clause of [def-exc-excellent-ring], and the generic local ring of an integral scheme is its function field. Excellence of this finite-type fibre and of its affine quotients is [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. Write $j:U\to F$, $q:U\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. These are a locally closed immersion and a morphism between regular affine schemes. The virtual dimension of $q$ is $d_y$. Using [lem-per-regular-gysin-calculus] and the given $p_x$, take the composite
$$\Lambda_U(\delta_X(x)+d_y)[2\delta_X(x)+2d_y]\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Cl}_q}q^!\Lambda(\delta_X(x))[2\delta_X(x)]\xrightarrow{q^!(p_x^{-1})}q^!R\Gamma_xK\cong j^!\pi^!R\Gamma_xK.$$
Its generic restriction is an isomorphism with target $R\Gamma_y(f^!K)$ by the costalk comparison; define $p_y^f$ to be its inverse. This pins the actual adjoint object, without selecting another dualizing complex.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 4.4.1, first paragraph and displayed Gysin construction

proof.text: Two choices of $U$ have a common nonempty affine open in their intersection containing $y$. Open-restriction compatibility of $\operatorname{Cl}_q$ in [lem-per-regular-gysin-calculus] and of the comparison in [lem-per-exceptional-costalk-calculus] identifies the two displayed composites there. Their generic restrictions, hence $p_y^f$, are equal. The same calculation on a smaller open chart in $Y$ or $X$ gives its restriction compatibility. Thus the pinnings are globally defined and can be tested in any affine neighbourhood of an immediate specialization.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 4.4.1, independence of the regular open

proof.text: For composition, let $Z\xrightarrow{g}Y\xrightarrow{f}X$ and fix $z\mapsto y\mapsto x$. Let $C_y$ and $C_z$ be the reduced closures of $y$ in $Y_x$ and of $z$ in $Z_x$. Since $g(z)=y$ and $C_z$ is reduced, $g$ maps $C_z$ into $C_y$. Take $U\subset C_y$ as in Step 2, with $q:U\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. The regular locus of $C_z$ is open by J-2 [def-exc-excellent-ring, lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], so we may choose a regular affine open $W\subset C_z$ containing $z$ inside $g^{-1}(U)$; write $r:W\to U$. Then $qr$ is a Step 2 model for $(fg)^!K$ at $z$. Since $U\to Y$ is a monomorphism, $W_\eta=W\times_U\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)=W\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ is a reduced irreducible locally closed subscheme of the fibre of $g$ over $y$ with generic point $z$, hence an open of the reduced closure of $z$ there; it is affine, regular (a localization of $W$) and of finite type over $\kappa(y)$. So $s=r_\eta:W_\eta\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ is a Step 2 model for $g^!(f^!K)$ at $z$, and by the localization clause of [lem-per-regular-gysin-calculus] $\operatorname{Cl}_s$ is the restriction of $\operatorname{Cl}_r$. By the composition clause, $\operatorname{Cl}_{qr}=r^!(\operatorname{Cl}_q)\circ\operatorname{Cl}_r(d_{y/x})[2d_{y/x}]$. Restricting $r^!$ to the generic fibre of $U$ is $s^!$ of the generic restriction [lem-per-exceptional-costalk-calculus], so at $z$ the successive inverse pinning $\operatorname{Cl}_s\circ s^!(\text{inverse of }p^f_y)$ is the generic restriction of $\operatorname{Cl}_r\circ r^!(\operatorname{Cl}_q\circ q^!(p_x^{-1}))$, which equals that of $\operatorname{Cl}_{qr}\circ(qr)^!(p_x^{-1})$, the inverse of the $(fg)$-pinning. The twist exponents add by [lem-exc-domain-transcendence-degree-tower]. Step 3 removes dependence on $U$ and $W$. Transitivity is the mate of compact-support composition [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] (compose the Hom bijections of the adjunctions).

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 4.4.1, composition assertion; Remark 4.1.3; Gysin composition

proof.text: If $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ is a closed immersion, its fibre at any point of its image is the same residue field. In Step 2 the class for this identity field map is the identity by [lem-per-regular-gysin-calculus]. Hence its pinnings are exactly the original costalk pinnings under [lem-per-exceptional-costalk-calculus]. Every immediate specialization in $Z$ is immediate in $Y$: every intermediate point would remain in the closed subset $|Z|$. The same costalk lemma identifies its residue transition. Thus the equation $p_{z'}=p_z(1)[2]\circ\operatorname{sp}_{z',z}$ for $K$ is exactly that for $i^!K$ [def-per-potential-dualizing]. Closed exceptional restriction therefore preserves potentiality, including nonregular or nonreduced $Z$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Definition 1.4.1 and final paragraph of Section 4.4

proof.text:
Let $p:P\to X$ be smooth, separated and compactifiable, of constant relative dimension $d$ (as $\mathbf A^n_W\to W$ in Step 7). It is regular, so [lem-per-regular-potential-pullback] makes $p^*K$ potential for
$$\delta_{\mathrm{reg}}(t)=\delta_X(p(t))-\dim\mathcal O_{P_{p(t)},t}.$$
The finite-type field dimension formula [lem-kun-dimension-formula] identifies $\dim\mathcal O_{P_{p(t)},t}+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(p(t))}\kappa(t)$ with $d$. Hence $\delta_P=\delta_{\mathrm{reg}}+d$. Tensor by $\Lambda(d)[2d]$: the costalk pinnings and transition equation in [def-per-potential-dualizing] are shifted by $(d)[2d]$ on both sides, so $p^*K(d)[2d]$ is potential for $\delta_P$. The normalized smooth isomorphism of [lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation] identifies this object with $p^!K$. Its pinnings agree with Step 2: on each fibre use the regular Gysin pinning from [lem-per-regular-potential-pullback], then compose its point Gysin class with the smooth orientation. Gysin composition and regular-base-change compatibility in [lem-per-regular-gysin-calculus] identify this composite with the class used on the regular open of the point closure in Step 2. The costalk comparison is [lem-per-exceptional-costalk-calculus]. Thus the prescribed pinnings, not just an unpinned isomorphism class, are potential.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 4.4.1, smooth comparison; Proposition 4.1.1. Correct convention: p^!K = p^*K(d)[2d]

proof.text:
Now take an immediate specialization in $Y$. Choose affine neighbourhoods $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of its specialization and $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of its image, with $f(V)\subset W$. Since $B$ is a finite-type $R$-algebra, choose generators $b_1,\ldots,b_n$. The surjection $R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$ gives
$$V\xrightarrow{i}\mathbf A^n_W\xrightarrow{p}W,$$
with $i$ closed [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-affine-space]. The ambient affine space is excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] and smooth of pure dimension $n$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. The open restriction of $K$ is potential, by its costalk definition [def-per-potential-dualizing] and the localization comparisons [lem-per-exceptional-costalk-calculus]. Step 6 makes $p^!K$ potential, and Step 5 makes $i^!p^!K$ potential. Step 4 identifies its pinnings with those of $f^!K$ on $V$. The chosen specialization therefore satisfies the transition equation. As it was arbitrary, $f^!K$ is potential. Empty schemes and $n=0$ cause no exception: there are then no points to pin, or the affine-space projection is the identity.
